ops.title: v0.55.0 appex probe-hammer STILL live on yBook-Pro (26x churn) + acct-16 -1005 launch gate — contradicts ship-note 89382e69 validation
ops.body:
Machine: **yBook-Pro.local** (primary Mac). Recorded 2026-07-14 ~14:05 PDT while on cc-pool v0.55.0 (18d5a45), daemon+bridge+app all restarted onto v0.55.0 at 12:33–12:37. Contradicts the clean-validation claim in note **89382e69** ("idle appex launches 2/5min; 0 sandbox-extension failures") — the ENOMEM half is fixed, the probe-hammer half is NOT, on this machine.

## Two live symptoms
1. **acct-16 launch-gate failure (13:36:31):** `ccp run` (pin-held select → acct-16) failed the P7 launch gate:
   `file provider prepare domain .../acct-16: prepare domain acct-16: file provider domain did not serve an enumeration in time: prepare-domain download settings.json for acct-16: NSFileProviderErrorDomain -1005: The file doesn't exist.` User re-ran → landed acct-13 (fine). **The file exists** — `~/.cc-pool/accounts/acct-16/settings.json` = 11208 B and the mount `~/Library/CloudStorage/CCPoolStatus-acct-16/settings.json` reads 11208 B right now. So the -1005 was **transient**, almost certainly the prepare-domain materialize racing the ongoing appex churn (the domain's appex was being torn down mid-download). Error path: `internal/cli/run.go:78` (`ErrDomainNotServing`, non-forced arm) ← fusekit `fileproviderd/control.go:197`.

2. **Appex respawn storm — the real problem, still live:**
   - **~53 unique `CCPoolFileProvider` appex PIDs launched per 5 min** (unified log, measured 14:00). Ship-note validated baseline was **~2 per 5 min → this is ~26×.**
   - ~58 spawn/teardown lifecycle events/min in category `XPCErrors` (Alloc + "Connection invalidated"), continuous.
   - Onset **~09:35–09:40 today**, still on v0.54.0 (04ce289). My spawn/invalidate metric was **0** every window overnight (22:30, 03:00, 04:40, 06:00, 09:00, 09:20–09:35) then jumped to 364 in 09:40–09:55, and has never stopped since — spanning the 12:37 v0.55.0 daemon restart with no change.

## Reconciliation (the apparent contradiction resolves cleanly)
- **OLD failure mode = ENOMEM** (fileproviderd "Failed to consume sandbox extension … errno=[12] Cannot allocate memory"), onset 2026-07-13 23:45 per note **0a067986**. **This is fixed: 0 occurrences in the last 12 min.** Appexes now launch successfully.
- **The probe-hammer that caused it is NOT gone.** v0.55.0's design intent (note 0a067986 fix directions; commits 566f1591 P0 shallow/deep cadence, 2720e9b4 widget shallow op) was to stop the 10s materializing deep-probe from waking every appex — targeting ~2 launches/5min (deep only, every 5m). On this machine appexes are still being woken at a ~10s-cadence rate (26×). The failure mode merely shifted from "launch fails (ENOMEM)" to "launch succeeds then is torn down and relaunched." Same hammer; memory pressure eased ~09:35 so launches started succeeding (which is exactly when my launch/invalidate metric lit up).
- Secondary fallout: the constant appex spawn/die makes `procscan` (KERN_PROCARGS2) frequently hit a just-exited PID → EIO → **aborts the whole scan** ("treating all accounts as busy this tick", "preflight refresh skipped", "hostsync List busy check … scan sessions"). Degrades session detection / refresh / widget reaping. Per-pid EIO should be skipped, not fatal to the scan.

## Also observed
- Companion app `CCPoolStatus` (PID 95650) is itself issuing `com.apple.FileProvider` XPC (`CFURLResolveBookmarkData`→container lookup→activating connection→cancelled) at **~12–18/sec in bursts** — far above what servicing a 10s×13-domain daemon probe would need (~1.3/sec). Suggests an app/widget-side loop (signalAllDomains / rehydrate / timeline reload / retry) is a second, independent driver. **Unconfirmed — needs the Swift-side trace.**

## Open diagnostic questions (were being traced when the workflow was stopped)
1. Is the v0.55.0 **shallow** probe actually zero-spawn on this machine, or is it still doing a materializing read (waking the appex) every 10s? i.e. did the fix regress/not-take here, or is the daemon falling back to deep probes (wedge/parked re-probe ladder hammering)? Correlate daemon probe ticks ↔ appex spawn waves.
2. What is the app's ~12–18/sec FileProvider XPC loop? (widget/appex Swift trace)
3. Confirm -1005 is the transient-during-churn race vs. deferred risk **W-X1** (note 22128082: prepare-domain accepts stale-but-materialized replica; not an exact match for "file doesn't exist").
4. procscan per-pid EIO tolerance (skip the pid vs abort the scan).

## Resume path
A stopped diagnosis workflow has these 4 traces queued (1 of 5 — the history/commit trace — already cached): `Workflow({scriptPath: "…/workflows/scripts/fp-churn-diagnosis-wf_03bb3d3b-b5a.js", resumeFromRunId: "wf_03bb3d3b-b5a"})`. Remaining agents route to codex-wrapper: cc-pool Go (run.go prepare + fpheal cadence), widget Swift (probeDomain shallow/deep + prepare-domain -1005 source + app XPC loop), fusekit (ProbeDomainShallow/PrepareDomain + v1.0.2..v1.1.0 diff), procscan (EIO abort).

## Mitigation options (NOT yet taken — evidence doesn't yet pin one, and the machine has live sessions)
- Bounce the companion app / `brew services restart cc-pool` — may reset an app-side loop, but won't fix a daemon shallow-probe regression; and `ccp service install` can leave the old daemon running (memory: fp-domains-finder-locations).
- acct-16 is currently serving fine; no per-account action needed for it specifically. The storm is fleet-wide, not acct-16-specific.
- Do NOT migrate off FP. Do NOT run authdb/tccutil cleanup.

Cross-refs: [[89382e69]] (ship+validation, contradicted here), [[0a067986]] (ENOMEM root cause + probe-hammer mechanism), [[22128082]] (Stage-2 verdict; W-X1), auto-memory fp-edeadlk-v0550-train.
